newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says coal asset sale report speculative.
newsitem.headline: BHP says coal asset sale report speculative.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd on Tuesday dismissed as speculative a report which said the company was likely to sell its interest in three Queensland coal mines.

"We have been reviewing all of our coal assets but as far as Queensland mines are concerned we haven't made firm decisions on any of these sites. We would view that as analyst speculation," a spokesman for the company told Reuters.

The report in The Australian newspaper said the company was believed to have approached joint venture partners to secure consent to sell its interest in the predominantly thermal-coal operations at Blackwater, Moura and South Walker Creek.

BHP has previously signalled its intention to focus on the coking coal market and announced in mid-June it would spend A$500 million expanding the Peak Downs and Sarji open-cut coking coal mines in Queensland and the port of Hays Point.
Blackwater is a part of the Central Queensland Coal Associates (CQCA) joint venture where BHP's partners include QCT Resources Ltd, Mitsubishi Development and the AMP Society.
BHP owns 80 percent of Moura and South Walker Creek which are a joint venture with Japanese group Mitsui.
In early June, the Australian Financial Review newspaper reported that BHP planned to sell its Mt Owen thermal coal mine in the Hunter Valley in New South Wales.
